lines.text: Two divers surfaced at the Great Barrier Reef. Their boat was gone.
January 1998. St Crispin's Reef, off Port Douglas.
Tom and Eileen Lonergan, experienced American divers.
Before leaving, the Outer Edge crew reportedly counted heads.
By one account, two other divers were counted twice.
On paper, everyone was aboard. The boat headed home.
Two days later, the crew found their bag still aboard.
Only then did the search begin.
Searchers found their gear. Not them.
A buoyancy vest washed ashore up the coast. Then a wetsuit.
Months later, a dive slate, reportedly asking for rescue.
Tom and Eileen were never found.
What happened in the water is unknown.
The skipper was acquitted. The company was fined and closed.
Queensland tightened its rules. Divers must now be counted twice, independently.
Because one wrong count is all it takes...
